rule: Appointment slots must be generated from operating hours, bay capacity, technician availability, and service duration templates.
example: An A/C repair cannot be offered into a 30-minute slot or outside the A/C specialist's shift.
exception: Manager may open a manual slot with explicit override reason.
system_response: Reject or suppress invalid slots; log overrides.

rule: Appointments requiring specialist skills must only be booked into slots where at least one qualified technician is scheduled.
example: Transmission diagnostics only appear on days when a transmission-qualified technician is present.
exception: Diagnostic-only holding slot may be created if policy allows later reassignment.
system_response: Offer only compatible slots or require override.

rule: Critical-parts services should not be confirmed unless mandatory parts are available, reservable, or a manager override is recorded.
example: Brake pad replacement is not confirmed without reserved pads and rotors if required.
exception: Diagnostic-only booking may proceed without parts reservation.
system_response: Flag as parts-pending or require override with reason.

rule: Multiple services requested for the same customer/vehicle in the same visit must be grouped under one appointment and one operational visit.
example: Oil change + tire rotation uses one appointment and one queue position.
exception: Separate days or separate vehicles create separate visits.
system_response: Merge requested lines into one visit plan.

rule: A customer only enters the active queue after check-in is completed by staff or approved self-check-in.
example: Booked customer arrives but is not eligible for ranking until check-in is done.
exception: Pre-arrival status may be visible for operational awareness but is not rankable.
system_response: Create or activate service visit and queue ticket at check-in.

rule: An appointment checked in from 30 minutes before to 15 minutes after its scheduled start retains protected appointment priority.
example: 9:00 AM appointment checked in at 8:45 AM or 9:10 AM remains protected.
exception: If parts or qualified technician are unavailable, visit becomes blocked rather than scheduled.
system_response: Assign priority class APPT_PROTECTED.

rule: Arrivals more than 30 minutes early are treated as walk-ins until the appointment protection window opens.
example: 10:00 AM appointment arriving at 9:00 AM may be served early only if walk-in rules permit.
exception: Manager may manually honor early protected treatment.
system_response: Assign temporary walk-in class until T-30 minutes.

rule: Appointments checked in 16 to 30 minutes late lose protected slot priority and enter the dynamic queue with a lateness penalty.
example: 9:00 AM appointment checked in at 9:22 AM no longer preempts all walk-ins.
exception: Manager may restore protected status for valid reasons.
system_response: Assign priority class APPT_LATE_SOFT and recompute ETA.

rule: Appointments more than 30 minutes late without approved exception become missed appointments and must be rescheduled or converted to walk-in service based on capacity.
example: 9:00 AM appointment arriving at 9:40 AM becomes MISSED unless staff override.
exception: Customer notified ahead due to emergency and manager approves same-day fit-in.
system_response: Mark appointment MISSED and offer reschedule or walk-in conversion.

rule: Walk-ins receive the next available immutable ticket number at the moment of completed check-in.
example: Two walk-ins arriving minutes apart receive ticket 014 and 015 even if rank later changes.
exception: None.
system_response: Create queue ticket and compute dynamic rank separately.

rule: If the same customer has multiple same-day services or appointments for the same vehicle, only one active queue position is allowed.
example: Brake inspection followed by oil change stays in one queue position with multiple order lines.
exception: Different vehicles may have separate visits.
system_response: Merge or link visits and prevent duplicate queue entries.

rule: Ticket number is immutable; queue rank is dynamic and recalculated as operating conditions change.
example: Ticket 018 may move from rank 6 to rank 4 after parts become ready.
exception: None.
system_response: Store sequence and rank as separate fields.

rule: Queue rank must be recomputed on check-in, technician availability changes, service completion, parts readiness changes, and manager override.
example: When a technician finishes a brake job, all eligible brake-family tickets may be resequenced.
exception: System maintenance mode may pause recomputation.
system_response: Trigger scheduler and persist decision snapshot.

rule: Eligible protected appointments rank ahead of eligible walk-ins.
example: An on-time 10:00 AM appointment outranks a 9:50 AM walk-in when both are ready and compatible.
exception: Quick-service fast-track lane may take qualifying walk-ins if no protected appointment is delayed beyond policy threshold.
system_response: Base priority class weighting enforces appointment preference.

rule: The system must surface long-wait walk-ins for manual review once wait time breaches the fairness threshold.
example: A walk-in waiting 90+ minutes triggers manager alert.
exception: None.
system_response: Create fairness alert and optional override suggestion.

rule: Quick-service visits may be fast-tracked only when a dedicated quick lane exists or when insertion will not delay any protected appointment by more than 10 minutes.
example: An oil change can jump ahead if a lube bay is idle.
exception: Manager may force insertion for strategic/VIP reasons with audit.
system_response: Apply quick-service bonus subject to delay constraint.

rule: Batching similar service families is allowed when it increases operational efficiency without violating protected appointment delay thresholds.
example: Three tire rotations may be grouped for one technician if promised times still hold.
exception: Safety-critical or customer-promised expedite jobs may bypass batch.
system_response: Apply batching bonus and record reason code.

rule: Every manual queue override requires a reason code, actor identity, and before/after snapshot.
example: Manager pushes a fleet customer ahead due to commercial SLA.
exception: None.
system_response: Persist audit log and status history.

rule: A technician may only be assigned when the required skill set is met.
example: Electrical diagnostic cannot be assigned to a lube-only technician.
exception: Trainee shadowing is allowed only with a qualified primary technician.
system_response: Block incompatible assignment.

rule: Complex repairs must be assigned to named specialists or technicians meeting the configured proficiency threshold.
example: A/C repair requires AC skill and proficiency level >= configured minimum.
exception: Manager temporary assignment with explicit supervision flag.
system_response: Filter assignment candidates by skill and level.

rule: A technician cannot be double-booked across overlapping active work unless one job is paused and the system records the pause.
example: Tech cannot be shown as actively performing two repairs at once.
exception: Inspection plus admin note tasks do not count as active wrench time.
system_response: Prevent overlapping active assignments.

rule: Work bay type must match the service requirement.
example: Wheel alignment must be assigned to an alignment-capable bay.
exception: No exception for mandatory bay requirements.
system_response: Exclude incompatible bays from scheduling.

rule: Mandatory parts requests must be created no later than advisor approval of the repair scope.
example: Brake replacement approval creates a request for pads, clips, and optional sensors.
exception: Diagnostic visits with unknown required parts.
system_response: Generate parts request and line items.

rule: For next-day appointments, missing critical parts must generate transfer or procurement action before the previous-business-day cutoff.
example: A 10:00 AM next-day appointment missing AC compressor triggers transfer by 3:00 PM prior day.
exception: Weekend/holiday cutoff uses preceding business day rules.
system_response: Open inventory transfer or procurement task and alert parts team.

rule: A job cannot move into Ready for Service when mandatory parts are unavailable, unless it is flagged diagnostic-only or overridden by manager.
example: Shock replacement remains BLOCKED_PARTS until shocks are reserved.
exception: Customer approves partial work order.
system_response: Block service-start state transition.

rule: Parts substitutions require advisor or manager approval and must be auditable.
example: Alternative oil filter brand used due to stock issue.
exception: Pre-approved equivalent substitute list can auto-approve.
system_response: Record substitution approval and update request item.

rule: Inventory transfers must track origin, destination, ETA, received timestamp, and exception reason if delayed.
example: Pads transferred from branch A to service center.
exception: None.
system_response: Expose transfer status in parts dashboard.

rule: Customer transport is available only to eligible services, eligible geography, and available transport capacity.
example: A 3-hour AC repair within the service zone qualifies for work drop-off.
exception: Manager may approve courtesy transport manually.
system_response: Eligibility checked at booking and reconfirmed at check-in.

rule: Drop-off destination and pickup preference must be confirmed before vehicle service start.
example: Customer chooses office drop-off and home pickup.
exception: Customer declines return pickup.
system_response: Store transport legs and required contact details.

rule: Return pickup coordination starts when predicted remaining service time is 30 minutes or less or when vehicle reaches Ready for Pickup.
example: System prompts dispatcher to contact customer near completion.
exception: Customer opted out of transport notifications.
system_response: Create dispatch alert and notification job.

rule: Driver assignment cannot occur without confirmed customer time window.
example: Dispatcher cannot assign driver until customer accepts 5:30 PM pickup window.
exception: Internal shuttle moves without customer if vehicle-only transfer.
system_response: Hold request in CONFIRMATION_PENDING.

rule: Booking confirmation must be sent immediately after appointment creation or reschedule.
example: Customer receives SMS/email with date, time, service summary, and instructions.
exception: Customer opted out or channel unavailable.
system_response: Queue notification with fallback channel if configured.

rule: Reminder cadence should default to 24 hours and 2 hours before appointment time.
example: Reminder sent day before and same morning.
exception: Same-day bookings skip 24-hour reminder.
system_response: Create scheduled jobs using job scheduler.

rule: Delay alerts must be sent when predicted start or completion breaches promised window by more than 15 minutes.
example: Technician delay pushes expected completion from 3:00 PM to 3:30 PM.
exception: Internal-only note when customer has no preferred channel.
system_response: Send proactive update and record delivery status.

rule: Every state change for appointments, visits, queue tickets, service orders, parts requests, and transport requests must be timestamped and auditable.
example: Service order moved from IN_PROGRESS to WAITING_PARTS.
exception: None.
system_response: Write to status_history automatically.

rule: Only managers and admins may edit global business rules, service durations, grace periods, or operating hours.
example: Technician cannot change 15-minute grace period.
exception: Feature-flagged delegated admin role may be introduced later.
system_response: Enforce RBAC and audit change.

rule: Operational records should be soft-deleted only when legally and operationally safe; otherwise use cancel/void states.
example: Cancelled appointment remains in history.
exception: PII deletion requests may require anonymization.
system_response: Use status-based lifecycle, not hard delete, for operational entities.

rule: External integration calls must be idempotent and retryable with dead-letter handling.
example: POS sync retries after temporary outage without creating duplicate invoices.
exception: None.
system_response: Use idempotency key and outbox/integration job tracking.

rule: Vehicle release should require payment cleared or approved account exception before final closure.
example: Cashier cannot close order until POS confirms payment.
exception: Charge account / fleet account with approved terms.
system_response: Block final close or mark on-account exception.
